input: adding a project. take clothes from dryer and put it on a hanger if it can be pressed better. universally puts things on a hanger. hangers can be custom designed. to design in a feedback sim loop. long term project. (follow-up: it's a robotics project that takes clothes out of the drier or from a loader and hangs them all on hangers.)
errors: experiments/run.py keyed results on id() of objects returned from a multiprocessing pool; the copies have new ids (KeyError). Fixed by keying on the frozen dataclass itself.
First L-BFGS start (horizontal cloth swinging down) needed >4000 iterations; starting from the cloth lying on the arm converged in ~300.
integrity_issues: First full run scored shape error only and the optimiser converged on wire-thin hanger ends (specification gaming); kept as results_shape_only.txt and reported as section G, main results use a crease-penalised objective.
Custom per-size CMA-ES (budget 150) did worse than the pooled adjustable-width search; README says B is budget-limited rather than a floor.
Fabric constants, garment weights and stock hanger dimensions are assumptions, stated as such; references not re-checked online.

doc_friction.issue: Adding a track still touches PROJECTS.md header and table, pick_track.py (PREFIX, constant in two places and docstring), prompts/research/prompt-0.md and prompt-1.md track count, projects.json theme and template.html colours; no checklist lists them together (also reported 2026-10-19 by another run).
Mixed indentation; json.dump re-serialisation rewrites hundreds of unrelated lines, so new themes must be inserted textually.
A new project pushed before its README and projects.json entry fails both the homepage check and ~9 platform/pages build tests; worth saying so to avoid chasing the build failures.

deviations.why: Owner asked to add a new long-term project, so this run added track 18 and its first milestone instead of drawing a track with pick_track.py.

goal: Add the owner's laundry-hanging robot as a research track and ship its first sim-loop result.
notes: Track 18 (hanger) added with 8 milestones. hanger-fit: 2D drape model + CMA-ES; one fixed hanger 2.11 cm mean shape error vs adjustable-width 0.176 cm, rack of 4 widths 0.51 cm; CMA-ES 0.19 vs random 0.44 cm at 150 drapes.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: researcher building a 2D cloth drape solver, CMA-ES loop, experiments and write-up from scratch, plus track spec

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
